_comment: Mutation testing: injects bugs into source, then checks whether the test suite notices. Coverage says a line RAN; this says the line is actually ASSERTED. Scoped to pure-logic modules that already have real coverage — mutating untested files just reports 0% and tells you nothing you didn't know from the coverage report.
_data_modules_comment: lib/routes.js, lib/schema.js, and lib/content/posts.js are deliberately NOT mutated. posts.js is mostly a zod schema declaration, whose mutants are boundary swaps (.max(80) -> .min(80)) and regex tweaks — killing them means asserting every bound of every field in both directions, which detects edits rather than defects. Its real logic (readingMinutes, assertNoRawScript, sorting, draft filtering, UTC date handling) is asserted directly and thoroughly in posts.test.js. Note also that both post test files do fs reads and page rendering at module scope, which coverageAnalysis:perTest cannot attribute to a test, so the reported score understates the real coverage. The rest: They are data: static object literals whose every surviving mutant is a swapped string ('Tarazu' -> ''). Killing those requires asserting each literal, which is a change-detector test that finds no defects and just makes the files annoying to edit. Their real invariants — @id cross-references resolving, description length bounds, the registry matching the filesystem, escape-safety of serialize() — are asserted in lib/schema.test.js and lib/routes.test.js, which is where the value actually is. Revisit lib/routes.js once navGroups() has real nav data to exercise.
_thresholds_comment: break is the ratchet: the run fails below it. Set to 90 against a measured 93.86%, leaving ~4 points of slack — some mutants are killed by test timeout rather than assertion failure, which moves the score by about a point between runs, so a threshold set at the current score would fail spuriously. Raise it as the score rises; never lower it to make a red build green.
